note: First meeting, written by the desk's Claude from tonight's packets. Press Run a fresh meeting for a live one, with a separate Claude in every seat.

posts.headline: Fear is high and the VIX curve is upside down, so expect big moves either way
posts.body: VIX closed at 26.4, higher than 95% of the past year and up about 50% in four weeks. The 3-month VIX (25.5) is now below it, which is an inverted curve. In past inversions the following week moved about 90% as much as VIX priced, against about 60% in calm times. Tomorrow's 80% range for the S&P is 7,028 to 7,379.
posts.watch: The curve going back above 1.0 (3-month VIX above VIX).
posts.change_mind: VIX back under 22 with the curve upright would say the storm is passing.

posts.headline: Bonds are acting as a safe place, but the bill market still prices a tighter Fed
posts.body: The 10-year fell 19 basis points in a week to 4.91% and the 2-year fell 17 to 4.63%, the usual move when stocks slide. But the 3-month bill at 4.36% sits above the Fed's 4.00% top rate, a one-year high, which reads like a market expecting another hike (my reading, not proven). Inflation expectations (2.12%) are at a one-year low while real yields (2.79%) are near a high.
posts.watch: Whether the 3-month bill falls back toward 4.00%.
posts.change_mind: Bills dropping under the Fed rate would mean the hike fear is gone.

posts.headline: Junk-bond spreads are the widest in a year; stress is building, not breaking
posts.body: High-yield spreads rose 54 basis points in 20 days to 3.72%, the top of their one-year range. Investment-grade spreads are also at a one-year high (0.98%). The St. Louis stress index jumped 0.80 in one week. The plumbing is still calm: SOFR 3.94%, fed funds 3.88%, and broad financial conditions (Chicago Fed, -0.44) are still looser than average.
posts.watch: High-yield spreads: a turn lower while VIX stays high is how past storms usually ended.
posts.change_mind: Spreads narrowing for a full week.

posts.headline: A tech-led selloff with money running to the dollar
posts.body: The Nasdaq is down 11.2% in 20 days, the S&P 6.8% and the Dow only 4.4%, so the damage is concentrated in tech. On the latest day the Dow rose while the Nasdaq fell. The broad dollar is at a one-year high and the loonie is at its weakest in a year (1.432 per US dollar). Oil fell 20% in a month to $82.
posts.watch: Nasdaq vs Dow: tech catching up would signal relief.
posts.change_mind: The dollar falling while stocks rise would say the safety bid is fading.

posts.headline: Look-alike days mostly bounced, but the bad tail is ugly
posts.body: The 150 days in history most like today (VIX near 26, S&P down about 2% in a week and 7% in a month, inverted curve) were up the next day 80% of the time, against 55% for all days. Over 5 days the median was +1.6%, but the worst 5% lost 4.3% or more. The two closest matches split: 26 Mar 2026 rose 10.6% in the next month, 6 Mar 2025 fell 6.0%.
posts.watch: Whether the next two sessions follow the analog bounce.
posts.change_mind: A new low in the S&P below 7,028 would push today toward the 2025 analog.

posts.headline: The room is telling stories; the numbers only support 'big moves, direction unknown'
posts.body: None of our seven analysts beats the plain up-rate, and over the last year the desk blend scored 0.2515 against 0.2513 for simply saying 55% every day. The look-alike signal History likes lost to the plain rate since 2022 (0.245 vs 0.244). Our new range rule held only 8 of the last 15 days. The board has not graded a single call yet. Data is also two days old because FRED lags.
posts.change_mind: Any signal beating the plain rate on new data.

debate.text: Your bounce cases mostly had spreads already turning down. Ours are still widening. I would not lean on the 80%.
Fair. I am not offering a direction call, only the spread of outcomes. The useful part is the size of the tail, not the 80%.
Yields fell while the dollar rose. So the dollar is not being pulled up by US rates, it is safety demand. That fits your tech story.
Agreed on direction. But the inverted curve is one of the few things that held up out of sample: moves stay big. That is worth saying plainly.
Four seats lean stormy, one leans bounce. Both are narratives. What we can defend: ranges stay wide, direction near a coin flip.

ceo.headline: A storm, not a crash: expect big moves both ways, with no proven edge on direction
lines: Bottom line: the next week should stay volatile. Direction is close to a coin flip, with the usual small up tilt (about 55%).
Why: VIX at 26 with an inverted curve, junk-bond spreads at a one-year high, and a Nasdaq-led drop of 11% in a month.

Where the room split: History sees a bounce (look-alikes up 80% next day); Red team notes that signal has never beaten the plain rate since 2022. I side with Red team on direction and with History on how big the bad tail can be.
One thing to watch: high-yield spreads. If they turn down while VIX stays high, past storms usually ended that way.
Housekeeping: the S&P's 80% range for the next session is 7,028 to 7,379, but our range rule held only 8 of the last 15 days, so treat the edges as soft.
